benchmark: Round455 matched full PPO replay with per-record public-mechanics static facts
finding: The public-mechanics static-facts cache reduced its isolated encoder median by 11.56% (48.27 to 42.69 ms) with exact feature parity. In the matched PPO replay, preparation took 161.79 s, 1.89 s lower than Round454 and 7.32 s below Round447. This is the fastest of the recent replay samples, but a single replay per code state cannot establish a stable speedup. Full update wall time from UTC start/completion timestamps rounded to seconds was about 224 s versus 228.6 s in Rounds453/454; do not treat this as a reliable end-to-end improvement. All 30 numeric metrics and all 82 model tensors matched Round447 exactly. Complete-iteration games/s remains 16.49 from Round430 because rollout generation was not measured here.
limitations: PPO update only; self-play rollout generation excluded. Wall time is rounded to whole UTC seconds from run-start and completion telemetry. Repeat matched replays to separate savings from run variation. Isolated public-mechanics timing excludes JSON parsing and other transition extraction.
